English 简体中文 
 

 a local gui for managing opencode configurations. toggle mcp servers, edit skills, manage plugins, handle auth - no json editing required. 

 
 
 
 

 
 
 

---

For the experimental production build and loopback-only Docker setup, see
production deployment. Remote use requires an
authenticated reverse proxy; the Studio backend has no remote authentication.

 opencode v2 configuration support

The compatibility work targets OpenCode 2.1.4 while retaining supported v1 config
editing. Studio preserves the source format instead of migrating your setup:

- Native agents and commands , including ordered permission rules and agent
 Markdown files; MCP's servers , disabled , and global timeout settings.
- Native provider model maps and plugin package entries/options.
- Both v1 and v2 usage database layouts, with errors instead of false zero totals
 when a database cannot be read.
- A separate Raw Config → v2 CLI editor for global cli.json . It does not
 overwrite tui.json or silently prevent first-launch migration.

Important limits: v2 authentication is metadata-only in Studio. Use opencode auth 
for credential changes and account selection; legacy Studio auth pools are not
applied to v2. V1 plugins need an actual API port, not a renamed config key. Native
plugin runtime controls use plugin IDs, so edit those controls in Raw Config rather
than relying on package-name toggles. Existing plugin code is never auto-converted.

See the compatibility verification notes and
upstream migration guide. End-to-end
native CLI agent discovery remains unverified; this is not a blanket compatibility
claim. Keep a backup, and do not point v1 at native-v2-only configuration.

---

 features

- mcp manager : toggle servers on/off, add new ones by pasting npx commands, delete unused configs
- profiles : isolated environments with separate configs, history, and sessions. switch instantly.
- skill editor : browse/edit skills, create from templates, import from url, bulk import multiple urls
- plugin hub : manage js/ts plugins, multiple templates (hooks, watchers, lifecycle), bulk import
- commands : browse and manage custom slash commands
- agents : manage custom agents with mode, model, tools, permissions (supports OMO format)
- usage dashboard : token costs, model breakdown, project stats from local message logs
- auth : login/logout per provider, save and switch between credential profiles
- github sync : push/pull config to a private github repo via gh cli
- backup/restore : export/import complete config including skills and plugins
- settings : general config, system prompt editor, oh my opencode model preferences
- i18n : internationalization support with Chinese (zh-CN) translation

---

 i18n (Internationalization)

OpenCode Studio supports multiple languages:

- English (default)
- Chinese (zh-CN) - 完整中文翻译

Language can be switched via the language switcher in the sidebar. Selection is saved in cookies and persists across sessions.

To add a new language:
1. Create client-next/messages/{locale}.json (e.g., ja.json for Japanese)
2. Copy structure from en.json and translate all keys
3. Add locale to client-next/src/i18n/request.ts 

---

 how it works

 

1. detect : server finds your opencode config directory automatically
2. read : loads opencode.json, skills, plugins, auth
3. edit : make changes through the ui
4. save : writes back to disk instantly

---

 deep links

opencode studio supports deep links for one-click installs from external sites.

 note : github blocks custom protocols like opencodestudio:// in user content. use a redirect page on github pages to bypass this.

 protocol description 
 :--- :--- 
 opencodestudio://launch start backend only 
 opencodestudio://launch?open=local start backend + open localhost:1080+ 
 opencodestudio://install-mcp?name=NAME&cmd=COMMAND install mcp server 
 opencodestudio://import-skill?url=URL import skill from url 
 opencodestudio://import-plugin?url=URL import plugin from url

 url encoding

parameters must be url-encoded:
- spaces → %20 
- / → %2F 
- : → %3A 
- { → %7B 
- } → %7D 

 security

when clicking deep links, users see a confirmation dialog showing the command or url and a warning about trusting the source.

---

 project structure

 

config locations:
- opencode config: /.config/opencode/ 
- studio data: /.config/opencode-studio/ 
- profiles: /.config/opencode-profiles/ 

---

 troubleshooting

 problem fix 
 :--- :--- 
 "opencode not found" ensure /.config/opencode/opencode.json exists 
 port conflicts both services auto-detect available ports (backend 1920+, frontend 1080+) 
 skills not showing check /.config/opencode/skill/ has SKILL.md files 
 bulk import fails ensure urls are raw github links 
 "Launch Backend" not working run npm install -g opencode-studio-server first 
 protocol handler not registered run opencode-studio-server --register as admin 
 github sync not working run gh auth login first 
 agents not showing (OMO) ensure oh-my-

For the experimental production build and loopback-only Docker setup, see production deployment. Remote use requires an authenticated reverse proxy; the Studio backend has no remote authentication.

opencode v2 configuration support

The compatibility work targets OpenCode 2.1.4 while retaining supported v1 config editing. Studio preserves the source format instead of migrating your setup:

  • Native agents and commands, including ordered permission rules and agent Markdown files; MCP's servers, disabled, and global timeout settings.
  • Native provider model maps and plugin package entries/options.
  • Both v1 and v2 usage database layouts, with errors instead of false zero totals when a database cannot be read.
  • A separate Raw Config → v2 CLI editor for global cli.json. It does not overwrite tui.json or silently prevent first-launch migration.

Important limits: v2 authentication is metadata-only in Studio. Use opencode auth for credential changes and account selection; legacy Studio auth pools are not applied to v2. V1 plugins need an actual API port, not a renamed config key. Native plugin runtime controls use plugin IDs, so edit those controls in Raw Config rather than relying on package-name toggles. Existing plugin code is never auto-converted.

See the compatibility verification notes and upstream migration guide. End-to-end native CLI agent discovery remains unverified; this is not a blanket compatibility claim. Keep a backup, and do not point v1 at native-v2-only configuration.
